rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi links human creation to 23:12–13, 64:2, 40:64, 95:4, and 96:2, arguing that decisive proofs establish the Lord alone creates every creature.
rows.anchor: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين * ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel's breathing is only a means through which God creates the soul and life; all ordinary causes likewise operate by God's origination, against naturalist doctrines.
rows.anchor: أي أن النفخ سبب خلق الله فيها الروح والحياة. وكذلك القول في سائر الأسباب المعتادة فإنه بإحداث الله تعالى

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that the soul is breathed into the fetus after 120 days, completing four months and entering the fifth, as established by the hadiths discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: لم يختلف العلماء أن نفخ الروح فيه يكون بعد مائة وعشرين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The certainty of fetal movement at this stage informs rulings on disputed paternity attribution and maintenance owed for a divorced woman's pregnancy.
rows.anchor: وعليه يعول فيما يحتاج إليه من الأحكام في الاستلحاق عند التنازع، وفي وجوب النفقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed wisdom for a widow's four-month-and-ten-day waiting period is that the interval establishes an empty womb if no pregnancy appears.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إنه الحكمة في عدة المرأة من الوفاة بأربعة أشهر وعشر

rows.speaker: مالك وأصحابه
rows.claim: A nutfa expelled before settling in the womb has no legal status; once it becomes a clot, expulsion of a clot or later-stage morsel counts as delivery, ending the waiting period and establishing umm walad status.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب مالك رضي الله عنه وأصحابه

words: ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i does not count an expelled clot; recognition of human form controls, and when a fleshy fetus has no visible form, two views are transmitted or derived, with the stated view ending idda but not making her umm walad.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه: لا اعتبار بإسقاط العلقة، وإنما الاعتبار بظهور الصورة والتخطيط

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra defines mukhallaqa as fully formed and ghayr mukhallaqa as a miscarriage.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: «مخلقة» تامة الخلق، «وغير مخلقة» السقط

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that if the term follows its root, the nutfa, clot, and morsel are all mukhallaqa because all are God's creation; the alternative imaging-based sense continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: إذا رجعنا إلى أصل الاشتقاق فإن النطفة والعلقة والمضغة مخلقة لأن الكل خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: If mukhallaqa means reaching the endpoint of formed appearance, Ibn al-Arabi identifies that interpretation with Ibn Zayd's account of developed body parts.
rows.anchor: فذلك ما قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers the broader derivation: takhliq means creating repeatedly, so every developmental stage, even a nutfa, is created and mukhallaqa; 23:14 supports successive creation.
rows.anchor: فما تتابع عليه الأطوار فقد خلق خلقا بعد خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view applies the contrast to individual children: God completes some fetuses' limbs while others are born premature and incomplete.
rows.anchor: منهم من يتم الرب سبحانه مضغته فيخلق له الأعضاء أجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes mukhallaqa to mean that the woman gives birth at full term.
rows.anchor: المخلقة أن تلد المرأة لتمام الوقت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines mukhallaqa as a living fetus and ghayr mukhallaqa as a miscarriage.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: المخلقة ما كان حيا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line asks why one should cry over the unformed miscarriage, illustrating the term's use.
rows.anchor: أفي غير المخلقة البكاء فأين الحزم ويحك والحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that an enslaved woman becomes umm walad if she miscarries a child fully formed.
rows.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أن الأمة تكون أم ولد بما تسقطه من ولد تام الخلق

rows.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي
rows.claim: Malik, al-Awza'i, and others establish umm walad status from a morsel whether formed or unformed, provided it is known to be a morsel.
rows.anchor: وعند مالك والأوزاعي وغيرهما بالمضغة كانت مخلقة أو غير مخلقة

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa establish umm walad status when any human feature, such as a finger or eye, is visible.
rows.anchor: إن كان قد تبين له شيء من خلق بني آدم أصبع أو عين

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي
rows.claim: The jurists agree that a newborn who cries aloud is prayed over; Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i, and others do not pray over one who does not cry.
rows.anchor: أجمعوا على أن المولود إذا استهل صارخا يصلى عليه فإن لم يستهل صارخا لم يصل عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن المسيب وابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Ibn Sirin, and others are reported to pray over a miscarriage even without the usual cry.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر أنه يصلى عليه وقاله ابن المسيب وابن سيرين وغيرهما

rows.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة
rows.claim: Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba ordered prayer, naming, washing, shrouding, and perfuming for miscarriages, saying Islam honors its young and old, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وروي عن المغيرة بن شعبة أنه كان يأمر بالصلاة على السقط

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi interprets al-Mughira's miscarriage as one with visible formation; an unformed loss, he says, has no existence.
rows.anchor: لعل المغيرة بن شعبة أراد بالسقط ما تبين خلقه فهو الذي يسمى

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say a miscarriage is prayed over once the soul has been breathed into it and four months are complete.
rows.anchor: يصلى عليه متى نفخ فيه الروح وتمت له أربعة أشهر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a newborn who cries aloud inherits.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري والأوزاعي والشافعي
rows.claim: For Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, and al-Shafi'i, movement, sneezing, breathing, or crying establishes life and inheritance.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب سفيان الثوري والأوزاعي والشافعي

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khattabi calls the position of the jurists of opinion the best view on signs of life for inheritance.
rows.anchor: قال الخطابي: وأحسنه قول أصحاب الرأي

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik denies inheritance absent a cry, even if the fetus moves or sneezes; this view is also transmitted from Ibn Sirin, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri, and Qatada.
rows.anchor: لا ميراث له وإن تحرك أو عطس ما لم يستهل صارخا

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik awards the ghurra for a morsel, clot, or known fetus miscarried after the woman's abdomen is struck.
rows.anchor: قال مالك رضي الله عنه: ما طرحته المرأة من مضغة أو علقة أو ما يعلم أنه ولد

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: For Malik, a miscarriage that does not cry brings the ghurra even if it moves or sneezes; a crying newborn brings full blood money.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: إذا سقط الجنين فلم يستهل صارخا ففيه الغرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي وسائر فقهاء الأمصار
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and jurists elsewhere require full blood money when movement, sneezing, crying, or another certain sign establishes the fetus was alive.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه وسائر فقهاء الأمصار: إذا علمت حياته بحركة أو بعطاس أو باستهلال

rows.speaker: القاضي إسماعيل
rows.claim: Qadi Isma'il says a miscarriage ends the woman's waiting period because it is a pregnancy, citing 65:4.
rows.anchor: التاسعة: ذكر القاضي إسماعيل أن عدة المرأة تنقضي بالسقط الموضوع

rows.speaker: القاضي إسماعيل
rows.claim: Qadi Isma'il's proof that the miscarried fetus existed as a child and pregnancy is that it inherits from its father.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي إسماعيل: والدليل على ذلك أنه يرث أباه، فدل على وجوده خلقا وكونه ولدا وحملا

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says none of these legal consequences attach unless the fetus is formed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: ولا يرتبط به شيء من هذه الأحكام إلا أن يكون مخلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi argues that the hadith about human formation in the womb and the language of pregnancy support ending idda when a clot or morsel settled in the womb is expelled, under 65:4.
rows.anchor: «إن أحدكم يجمع خلقه في بطن أمه» يدل على صحة ما قلناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expelled clot or morsel is the embryo's embodied beginning, like the outlined fetus, so the woman's claim to have been pregnant and delivered is evident.
rows.anchor: ولأنها وضعت مبدأ الولد عن نطفة متجسدا كالمخطط، وهذا بين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a miscarried child sent ahead is dearer to him than a horseman left behind; al-Hakim's version says a thousand horsemen.
rows.anchor: لسقط أقدمه بين يدي أحب إلي من فارس أخلفه خلفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lunubayyina means God displays the perfection of His power by moving human creation through its stages.
rows.anchor: { لنبين لكم } يريد: كمال قدرتنا بتصريفنا أطوار خلقكم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim transmits the accusative readings nuqirra and nukhrija from Asim through Abu Yazid and al-Mufaddal, parsing them by coordination.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: النصب على العطف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj insists on nominative nuqirru: creation is not for the purpose of keeping fetuses, but to guide people to right conduct; he takes the resurrection clarification as parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «نقر» بالرفع لا غير لأنه ليس المعنى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read nuqirru in the nominative, meaning, 'We keep in the wombs what We will.'
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: قراءة
rows.claim: A variant reads yuqirru and yukh'rijukum in the third person, with the nominative also valid in that reading.
rows.anchor: «ويقر» و«يخرجكم» بالياء، والرفع على هذا سائغ

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab reads the nun of nasha' with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب «ما نشاء» بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term differs for each fetus: some miscarry, while others complete development and emerge alive.
rows.anchor: والأجل المسمى يختلف بحسب جنين جنين فثم من يسقط وثم من يكمل أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ma rather than man refers to the pregnancy, including the morsel, which is inanimate.
rows.anchor: وقال «ما نشاء» ولم يقل من نشاء لأنه يرجع إلى الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tiflan is a generic singular used for the plural sense, 'as children'; it may also mean each one of you as a child.
rows.anchor: أي أطفالا فهو اسم جنس. وأيضا فإن العرب قد تسمي الجمع باسم الواحد

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet uses a singular noun for a plural group, as the line's plural reproaches are paired with the singular amir.
rows.anchor: يلحينني في حبها ويلمنني إن العواذل ليس لي بأمير

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says tifl can function as a verbal noun like rida and adl, applying to singular and plural; 24:31 gives another use.
rows.anchor: كالرضا والعدل، فيقع على الواحد والجمع قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari parses tiflan as an accusative of specification, comparing 4:4.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: وهو نصب على التمييز، كقوله تعالى: فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tifl applies from a child's separation at birth until puberty, and is also used for offspring of wild animals.
rows.anchor: والطفل يطلق من وقت انفصال الولد إلى البلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tifl can describe one or multiple girls or boys, and has dual and plural forms, but Arab usage does not say tiflat.
rows.anchor: طفل وطفلة وطفلان وطفلتان وأطفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atf alat means a woman has become a mother; mutfila describes a gazelle or camel with its young soon after birth, with plural forms mutafil and mutafil.
rows.anchor: والمطفلة: الظبية معها طفلها، وهي قريبة عهد بالنتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatHa on the ta, tifl means soft or delicate, as in a gentle girl or fingers.
rows.anchor: والطفل بالفتح في الطاء الناعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb tafila for night describes darkness beginning to fall.
rows.anchor: وقد طفل الليل إذا أقبل ظلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the noun's vowelled form, al-tifl denotes the time after midafternoon as the sun approaches sunset.
rows.anchor: بعد العصر إذا طفلت الشمس للغروب

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Tifl also means rain, as shown by the poetic phrase about a rain shower driven by the Pleiades.
rows.anchor: والطفل بالتحريك: بعد العصر إذا طفلت الشمس للغروب. والطفل أيضا: مطر قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat thumma as redundant, like the waw in 39:73.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن «ثم» زائدة كالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means mature intellect and the peak of physical strength.
rows.anchor: «أشدكم» كمال عقولكم ونهاية قواكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst age is senility and dementia, when a person loses understanding, so that after knowledge he knows nothing; compare 36:68.
rows.anchor: أي أخسه وأدونه وهو الهرم والخرف حتى لا يعقل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from miserliness, cowardice, returning to the worst age, worldly temptation, and grave punishment; al-Nasa'i reports it from Sa'd.
rows.anchor: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من البخل وأعوذ بك من الجبن وأعوذ بك أن أرد إلى أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: سعد
rows.claim: Sa'd says the Prophet taught these supplications to his sons as a teacher instructs boys.
rows.anchor: وكان يعلمهن بنيه كما يعلم المكتب الغلمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's revival offers stronger proof of resurrection: the wording shifts from plural addressees to a singular observer while the argument remains directed at resurrection-deniers.
rows.anchor: ذكر دلالة أقوى على البعث فقال في الأول: «فإنا خلقناكم من تراب»

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says hamida means dry and unable to grow anything.
rows.anchor: { هامدة } يابسة لا تنبت شيئا قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is dārisa, worn away; al-A'sha's verse about a pale body and worn clothes illustrates this usage.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دارسة. والهمود الدروس. قال الأعشى

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi glosses hamida as dry and soil-like.
rows.anchor: الهروي: «هامدة» أي جافة ذات تراب

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Shammar gives several senses: land's trees wither, voices fall silent, and soil is lifeless without vegetation or rain; garments wear out and fires subside.
rows.anchor: وهمود الأرض ألا يكون فيها حياة ولا نبت ولا عود ولم يصبها مطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the hadith phrase that hunger nearly makes someone yahmid, the verb means to perish.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: " حتى كاد يهمد من الجوع " أي يهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamida is also used of a garment becoming worn.
rows.anchor: يقال: همد الثوب يهمد إذا بلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihtazzat means moved vigorously; the earth is said to shake because growing plants subtly push its soil apart, a metaphorical usage.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت } أي تحركت. والاهتزاز: شدة الحركة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad instead takes the phrase as 'its plant shook,' with the genitive noun omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اهتز نباتها، فحذف المضاف قاله المبرد

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic simile compares a woman's movement while walking to the shaking of a leafy branch, illustrating plant-like movement.
rows.anchor: تثنى إذا قامت وتهتز إن مشت كما اهتز غصن البان في ورق خضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabat means rose, increased, or swelled; these explanations converge on increase, from the root r-b-w.
rows.anchor: { وربت } أي ارتفعت وزادت. وقيل: انتفخت والمعنى واحد، وأصله الزيادة

rows.speaker: يزيد بن القعقاع وخالد بن الياس
rows.claim: Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa and Khalid ibn Ilyas read raba'at with hamza, meaning it rose like a lookout on high ground; the derivative names the watchman.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن القعقاع وخالد بن الياس «وربأت» أي ارتفعت حتى صارت بمنزلة الربيئة

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays's line about sending a lookout witnesses the sense of rabī'a as a scout stationed above.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: بعثنا ربيئا قبل ذاك مخملا كذئب الغضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anbatat means the earth brought forth growth.
rows.anchor: { وأنبتت } أي أخرجت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj here means a color or kind.
rows.anchor: { من كل زوج } أي لون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses bahij as beautiful and pleasing to whoever sees it.
rows.anchor: { بهيج } أي حسن عن قتادة. أي يبهج من يراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse says the earth produces growth, Qurtubi concludes that 'shook and swelled' describes the earth, not the plants.
rows.anchor: ولما وصف الأرض بالإنبات دل على أن قوله: «اهتزت وربت» يرجع إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alam tara is a vision of the heart, meaning perception by heart and intellect.
rows.anchor: هذه رؤية القلب أي ألم تر بقلبك وعقلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is conjoined to man, and the moon, stars, mountains, trees, beasts, and many people follow the same construction.
rows.anchor: والشمس } معطوفة على «من». وكذا { والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra say accusative coordination would be good, but nominative is preferred because this begins a clause meaning many refuse prostration; the preceding clause ends at 'many people.'
rows.anchor: فزعم الكسائي والفراء أنه لو نصب لكان حسنا، ولكن اختير الرفع لأن المعنى وكثير أبى السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse coordinates the phrase if prostration means submission to God's ordering through weakness and strength, health and sickness, and beauty and ugliness, which applies to all.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معطوفا، على أن يكون السجود التذلل والانقياد لتدبير الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible accusative supplies an omitted verb: 'and He humbled many upon whom punishment is due.'
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب على تقدير: وأهان كثيرا حق عليه العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another parse ends the earlier sentence at beasts and takes the two groups as many people in Paradise and many destined for punishment; Ibn Abbas's explanation is cited by Ibn al-Anbari.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: المعنى وكثير من الناس في الجنة وكثير حق عليه العذاب

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says every star, moon, and sun prostrates to God at setting, then waits for permission to return to its rising place.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: ما في السموات نجم ولا قمر ولا شمس إلا يقع ساجدا لله حين يغيب

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says a sound-chain report describes the sun's real prostration, which entails life and intellect in the prostrating being.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: وورد هذا في خبر مسند في حق الشمس فهذا سجود حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi identifies the alluded-to sound-chain report as one Muslim transmitted and says it will be discussed at 36:38.
rows.anchor: قلت: الحديث المسند الذي أشار إليه خرجه مسلم، وسيأتي في سورة «يس»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God humiliates through wretchedness and unbelief has no one able to remove that humiliation.
rows.anchor: أي من أهانه بالشقاء والكفر لا يقدر أحد على دفع الهوان عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever treats worship of God lightly ends up in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن من تهاون بعبادة الله صار إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's doing what He wills means these people will end in Hell, and no one may object to Him.
rows.anchor: يريد أن مصيرهم إلى النار فلا اعتراض لأحد عليه

rows.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Kisa'i, and al-Farra explain mukrim as honoring or giving honor.
rows.anchor: وحكى الأخفش والكسائي والفراء «ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم» أي إكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers were expelled unjustly for professing that God alone is their Lord.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم } هذا أحد ما ظلموا به وإنما أخرجوا لقولهم: ربنا الله وحده

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh parses the exception as disconnected: they were expelled unjustly, but because they said, 'Our Lord is God.'
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن لقولهم ربنا الله قاله سيبويه

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra, with al-Zajjaj, allows a genitive construction returning to the preceding bi: they were expelled on account of monotheism by idolaters.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز أن تكون في موضع خفض، يقدرها مردودة على الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhina ukhriju is genitive as an appositive to alladhina yuqatilun.
rows.anchor: و { الذين أخرجوا } في موضع خفض بدلا من قوله: { للذين يقاتلون }

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that before the Aqaba pledge the Prophet had no permission to fight or shed blood; for ten years he called people to God, endured harm, and overlooked the ignorant, fulfilling the promise in 17:15.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل بيعة العقبة لم يؤذن له في الحرب ولم تحل له الدماء

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Quraysh persecuted the Prophet's migrant followers, tempted some away from faith, and drove them from home; some fled to Abyssinia, some to Medina, and some endured.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من فر إلى أرض الحبشة، ومنهم من خرج إلى المدينة، ومنهم من صبر على الأذى

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: After Quraysh rejected God's command, denied the Prophet, and tortured believers, God permitted fighting, self-defense, and resistance, revealing 22:39–40.
rows.anchor: وأنزل { أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا إلى قوله الأمور }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that a coerced act is attributed to the one who compels it: God ascribes the expulsion to the unbelievers to assign the blame.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن نسبة الفعل الموجود من الملجأ المكره إلى الذي ألجأه وأكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the same attribution is used in 9:40, 'when the unbelievers expelled him.'
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مثل قوله تعالى: إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed fighting for prophets and believers so polytheists would not take over and disable religious worship; required jihad lets adherents worship freely.
rows.anchor: أي لولا ما شرعه الله تعالى للأنبياء والمؤمنين من قتال الأعداء، لاستولى أهل الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihad preceded Islam among earlier communities and preserved their religious laws and places of worship; the verse strengthens the command to fight for truth.
rows.anchor: فالجهاد أمر متقدم في الأمم، وبه صلحت الشرائع واجتمعت المتعبدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christians or Sabians who condemn jihad contradict their own position, since without fighting the religions they defend would not have survived.
rows.anchor: فمن استبشع من النصارى والصابئين الجهاد فهو مناقض لمذهبه إذ لولا القتال لما بقي الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed sanctuaries existed before their communities' alterations and before Islam superseded those laws: churches under Moses, monasteries and churches under Jesus, and mosques under Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي لولا هذا الدفع لهدم في زمن موسى الكنائس، وفي زمن عيسى الصوامع والبيع

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the reading and interpretation as 'they would be demolished' is the soundest explanation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هذا أصوب ما قيل في تأويل الآية

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says God wards off unbelievers from later generations through Muhammad's Companions; Qurtubi accepts the general defense but says fighting fits the verse better.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال: ولولا دفع الله بأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says God wards off one people's oppression through the testimony of upright witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لولا دفع الله ظلم قوم بشهادة العدول

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says God wards off oppressors' wrongdoing through governors' justice.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ولولا دفع الله ظلم الظلمة بعدل الولاة

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda says God protects those outside mosques through mosque-goers and those who do not fight through those who fight, or punishment would come.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: لولا أن الله عز وجل يدفع بمن في المساجد عمن ليس في المساجد

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says God wards off punishment through the supplication of virtuous and righteous people; the verse necessarily implies both a defender and one defended.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ولولا دفع الله العذاب بدعاء الفضلاء والأخيار

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuzaymandad says the verse bars destroying protected non-Muslims' churches, synagogues, and fire temples in Muslim lands because the treaty protects them like their homes and property.
rows.anchor: تضمنت هذه الآية المنع من هدم كنائس أهل الذمة وبيعهم وبيوت نيرانهم

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: He says protected communities may not construct new sanctuaries or expand or heighten existing ones, and Muslims should not enter or pray there; additions must be demolished and temples in enemy territory may be destroyed.
rows.anchor: ولا يتركون أن يحدثوا ما لم يكن، ولا يزيدون في البنيان لا سعة ولا ارتفاعا

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: He allows a mosque to be demolished for rebuilding, citing Uthman's rebuilding of the Prophet's mosque.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن ينقض المسجد ليعاد بنيانه وقد فعل ذلك عثمان رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: قراءة
rows.claim: The verb is read with a light or doubled dal.
rows.anchor: قرىء «لهدمت» بتخفيف الدال وتشديدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawami is the plural of sawma'a, a tall structure pointed at the top, named from raising and sharpening the top of a thārid dish.
rows.anchor: { صوامع } جمع صومعة، وزنها فوعلة، وهي بناء مرتفع حديد الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also describes a sharp-hearted, keen-witted person or sharp speech; it can additionally denote a person or animal with a small ear.
rows.anchor: ورجل أصمع القلب أي حاد الفطنة. والأصمع من الرجال الحديد القول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says monasteries originally belonged to Christian monks and Sabian worshippers, then the term was used for Muslim minarets.
rows.anchor: وكانت قبل الإسلام مختصة برهبان النصارى وبعباد الصابئين قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biya' is the plural of bi'a, the Christian church.
rows.anchor: والبيع جمع بيعة، وهي كنيسة النصارى

rows.speaker: الزجاج والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Hasan identify salawat as Jewish synagogues, called salota in Aramaic.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج والحسن: هي كنائس اليهود وهي بالعبرانية صلوتا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says salawat are Christian prayer houses in the wilderness for travelers, called salota and Arabized as salawat.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الصلوات بيوت تبنى للنصارى في البراري يصلون فيها في أسفارهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya records nine readings of salawat, including salawat, salula, salub, and saluth, with further forms distinguished by vowel, consonant, and final spelling.
rows.anchor: وفي «صلوات» تسع قراءات ذكرها ابن عطية

rows.speaker: عاصم الجحدري والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas adds Asim al-Jahdari's salub and al-Dahhak's saluth, with the latter's sad vowel uncertain, bringing the total to twelve readings.
rows.anchor: وروى عن عاصم الجحدري أنه قرأ «وصلوب». وروي عن الضحاك «وصلوث» بالثاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says salawat are churches.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الصلوات الكنائس

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says salawat are the Sabians' mosques.
rows.anchor: أبو العالية: الصلوات مساجد الصابئين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes salawat as Muslims' prayer sites, whose worship is interrupted when enemies arrive; on this view 'demolished' is metaphorical for disabled worship or omits 'places of.'
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: هي صلوات المسلمين تنقطع إذا دخل عليهم العدو وتهدم المساجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والزجاج
rows.claim: On Ibn Abbas's and al-Zajjaj's explanations, destruction of the worship sites is literal.
rows.anchor: وعلى قول ابن عباس والزجاج وغيرهم يكون الهدم حقيقة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says demolishing salawat means abandoning them.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هدم الصلوات تركها

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub identifies salawat as small monasteries, with no singular form known.
rows.anchor: قطرب: هي الصوامع الصغار ولم يسمع لها واحد

rows.speaker: خصيف
rows.claim: Khasif assigns each name to a community's worship place: monasteries to monks, churches to Christians, salawat to Jews, and mosques to Muslims.
rows.anchor: فالصوامع للرهبان، والبيع للنصارى، والصلوات لليهود، والمساجد للمسلمين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers that the list rhetorically amplifies the range of worship sites; most names are shared across scriptural communities except bi'a, specifically Christian in Arabic.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والأظهر أنها قصد بها المبالغة في ذكر المتعبدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms concern ancient scriptural communities; Magians and polytheists are omitted because they have no sanctuaries requiring protection and do not invoke God's name as adherents of revealed laws do.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر في هذه الآية المجوس ولا أهل الإشراك لأن هؤلاء ليس لهم ما يجب حمايته

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says the pronoun in 'God's name is mentioned therein' should, by the nearest-noun rule, refer to mosques; it may instead refer to all listed sites during their laws and practice of truth.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: «يذكر فيها اسم الله» الذي يجب في كلام العرب على حقيقة النظر أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques and prayer sites of protected communities are placed first because they were older buildings.
rows.anchor: قيل: لأنها أقدم بناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the earlier sites are nearer destruction, while mosques are closer to remembrance; Qurtubi compares the delayed mention of the foremost in 35:32.
rows.anchor: وقيل لقربها من الهدم وقرب المساجد من الذكر كما أخر السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Helping God means helping His religion and His Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي من ينصر دينه ونبيه

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khattabi says strong can mean capable, since whoever is strong enough to do something can accomplish it.
rows.anchor: القوي يكون بمعنى القادر، ومن قوي على شيء فقد قدر عليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses aziz as exalted and noble.
rows.anchor: { عزيز } أي جليل شريف قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is the one who is inviolable and cannot be overcome, as Qurtubi explains in his book on the divine names.
rows.anchor: وقيل الممتنع الذي لا يرام وقد بيناهما في الكتاب الأسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mansakan means a prescribed law, and nasikuhu means those who practice it.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا } أي شرعا. { هم ناسكوه } أي عاملون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one should dispute with the Prophet about what is prescribed for his community, since laws differed in each era.
rows.anchor: { فلا ينازعنّك في الأمر } أي لا ينازعنك أحد منهم فيما يشرع لأمتك

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group reports that the verse answered pagans arguing that Muslims eat animals they slaughter but not carrion killed by God, claiming God's killing should be more worthy to eat.
rows.anchor: وروت فرقة أن هذه الآية نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار في أمر الذبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase indicates that mansak is an action or verbal noun: if it meant a place, it would say they are worshippers in it.
rows.anchor: { هم ناسكوه } يعطي أن المنسك المصدر، ولو كان الموضع لقال هم ناسكون فيه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses the phrase as 'let them not argue with you,' supported by the following mention of their arguing.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «فلا ينازعنك في الأمر» أي فلا يجادلنك ودل على هذا «وإن جادلوك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though opponents did dispute, the reciprocal form means 'do not dispute with them yourself'; it is like telling someone not to fight back when attacked.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال: لا يضربنك زيد وأنت تريد لا تضرب زيدا

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abu Mujliz reads falā yanza'nnaka, meaning do not let them snatch or overpower you and divert you from your religion; the common reading means disputing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز «فلا ينزعنك في الأمر» أي لا يستخفنك ولا يغلبنك عن دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings address the unbelievers while intending the Prophet as the recipient of the warning.
rows.anchor: ولفظ النهي في القراءتين للكفار، والمراد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling people to God's oneness, religion, and faith in Him.
rows.anchor: { وادع إلى ربك } أي إلى توحيده ودينه والإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is upon guidance, meaning a straight religion with no crookedness.
rows.anchor: { إنك لعلى هدى } أي دين. { مستقيم } أي قويم لا اعوجاج فيه
